items.title: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
items.summary: Open commerce protocol for interoperable journeys between consumer surfaces, businesses, agents, and payment providers. Supports API, MCP, and A2A bindings.
machine_notes: Shopify exposes UCP-shaped MCP tools for catalog, cart, checkout, and orders.

items.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
items.summary: Standard protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to AI applications. AgentCom uses MCP as its primary agent-facing query interface.
machine_notes: Current TypeScript SDK v2 implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification.

items.title: Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
items.summary: Open standard connecting buyers, AI agents, and businesses for product discovery and commerce interactions.
machine_notes: OpenAI expanded ACP to product discovery in 2026.

sources.title: OpenAI: Powering Product Discovery in ChatGPT

items.title: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
items.summary: Open protocol for secure, interoperable payments involving AI agents, designed to work alongside commerce and agent interoperability protocols.
machine_notes: AP2 can be used as an extension alongside A2A and UCP.

items.title: Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
items.summary: Open protocol for communication and interoperability between independent agentic applications.
machine_notes: A2A complements MCP: A2A connects agents to agents; MCP connects agents to tools and resources.

items.title: x402
items.summary: HTTP-native payments protocol centered on 402 Payment Required, with SDKs for machine and agent payments.
machine_notes: Useful for paid APIs, datasets, compute, and agent-to-service transactions.

items.title: Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)
items.summary: Open standard for machine-to-machine payments using an HTTP payment flow, designed for agentic payments and usage-based services.
machine_notes: Co-authored by Tempo and Stripe; supports agents paying for services without pre-created billing accounts.

items.title: Shopify
items.summary: The most mature mainstream merchant platform for UCP/MCP exposure in the current agentic-commerce stack.
quick_actions: Verify the managed /agents.md page.
Inspect /.well-known/ucp.
Test storefront catalog tools with an agent profile.
Keep policies, variants, inventory, and shipping data precise.

items.title: Google / Merchant Center
items.summary: Google is onboarding merchants to UCP-powered checkout surfaces in AI Mode and Gemini, with Merchant Center as an onboarding surface.
quick_actions: Maintain Merchant Center product data.
Review UCP technical implementation requirements.
Validate merchant identity and checkout readiness in the available onboarding sandbox.

items.title: OpenAI / ChatGPT Commerce
items.summary: ChatGPT shopping uses merchant/product metadata and ACP-based discovery integrations, including direct merchant feeds and platform integrations.
quick_actions: Ensure product data is complete and fresh.
If eligible, apply for direct product feed access.
For Shopify/Etsy merchants, confirm upstream catalog quality because those catalogs are integrated.

sources.title: OpenAI: Powering Product Discovery in ChatGPT

items.title: Stripe
items.summary: Stripe provides agentic-commerce infrastructure for product distribution, checkout/payments, agent wallets, and machine payments.
quick_actions: Map products/services into structured catalogs.
Choose agentic distribution channels.
Evaluate MPP for paid machine-accessible services.
Preserve transaction metadata and authorization trails.

items.title: TikTok Shop
items.summary: TikTok Shop exposes APIs for sellers and partners to create, update, retrieve, and synchronize structured product catalog data.
quick_actions: Keep product identifiers stable.
Synchronize title, description, price, inventory, and images.
Consume product review/update webhooks.
Treat the catalog as a machine-readable commerce source of truth.

items.title: Meta Commerce
items.summary: Meta Commerce Manager catalogs are structured product sources for Facebook and Instagram commerce and advertising surfaces.
quick_actions: Use a canonical catalog with stable IDs.
Keep product details and inventory current.
Resolve catalog diagnostics.
Preserve consistency between website product IDs and Meta catalog IDs.

items.title: Make a Shopify store agent-ready
items.summary: A practical checklist for Shopify merchants: agents.md, UCP discovery, catalog quality, policies, and transaction surfaces.
steps: Open /agents.md on the storefront and verify it accurately describes the store and commerce capabilities.
Open /.well-known/ucp and record the supported UCP version, capabilities, transport, and MCP endpoint.
Test catalog discovery against the store MCP endpoint using an agent profile URL.
Verify variant-level product facts: identifiers, price, currency, availability, media, and descriptions.
Make shipping, returns, contact, and fulfillment policies directly accessible and unambiguous.
Track agent referrals and checkout handoffs separately from ordinary browser traffic.

items.title: Prepare for Google UCP / Gemini commerce
items.summary: A merchant-oriented checklist for getting product data and checkout infrastructure ready for Google UCP onboarding.
steps: Keep Merchant Center account and product data compliant and current.
Implement the UCP technical requirements before expecting program onboarding.
Publish and validate the required UCP business profile and identity linkage.
Validate native checkout APIs in Google's onboarding/sandbox flow when your account receives access.
Model agent checkout as an extension of your merchant backend, not a separate storefront.

items.title: Prepare products for discovery in ChatGPT
items.summary: How to make merchant/product data complete, current, and suitable for ChatGPT shopping and ACP-based product discovery.
steps: Use stable product and variant identifiers across feeds and your storefront.
Keep price and availability synchronized frequently enough to avoid stale recommendations.
Provide specific attributes that help an agent satisfy constraints, not only marketing copy.
For direct-feed eligible merchants, follow OpenAI's current product feed specification and application flow.
For Shopify or Etsy, improve the upstream catalog because those platforms already provide product data to ChatGPT.
Measure assisted traffic and downstream conversion rather than only classic search rankings.

items.title: Agent SEO / ACO fundamentals
items.summary: A platform-neutral playbook for making a merchant legible, trustworthy, and actionable to AI agents.
steps: Expose stable, server-rendered facts: product identity, variants, price, availability, shipping, and policies.
Make machine entry points explicit: sitemap, structured data, llms.txt/agents.md where applicable, APIs, MCP, and protocol discovery files.
Use canonical identifiers consistently across website, feeds, marketplaces, and social catalogs.
Publish negative constraints as clearly as positive claims: exclusions, incompatibilities, delivery limitations, and return exceptions.
Keep mutable facts fresh and timestamped.
Create deterministic task paths for search, compare, cart, checkout, order lookup, returns, and support.
Test with agents and record failures as data-quality bugs.

items.title: Expose commerce knowledge through MCP
items.summary: Design an MCP server that gives agents authoritative commerce resources and narrowly-scoped tools.
steps: Expose read-only resources for policies, schemas, product definitions, and integration guidance.
Use tools only when the agent must compute, query fresh state, or cause an action.
Return structuredContent or JSON objects in addition to human-readable summaries.
Keep tool schemas narrow and explicit; never hide required parameters inside prose.
Separate public knowledge tools from authenticated merchant actions.
Version machine resources and include provenance.

items.title: Add machine payments with Stripe / MPP
items.summary: When and how to make an API, dataset, compute service, or agent-accessible endpoint payable by machines.
steps: Identify a unit that is naturally payable per request, session, result, or usage block.
Publish clear machine-readable pricing and what the payment unlocks.
Use MPP-compatible payment negotiation instead of requiring a human-created billing account where appropriate.
Design idempotency and receipts into paid tool calls.
Expose testnet/sandbox examples before production money movement.

items.title: Build a clean TikTok Shop product data pipeline
items.summary: Treat TikTok Shop as another structured commerce surface with synchronized product state and webhook-driven updates.
steps: Map your canonical SKU/variant model to TikTok Shop product records.
Synchronize title, description, media, pricing, inventory, and required sales terms.
Use create/edit APIs for controlled updates rather than manual drift.
Consume product webhooks to track review and state changes.
Record per-market differences in required product creation fields.

items.title: Create a canonical Meta Commerce catalog
items.summary: A baseline for keeping Facebook and Instagram commerce product data structured, stable, and synchronized.
steps: Create and own the catalog in the correct Meta business account.
Use stable product IDs that map back to canonical SKUs/variants.
Choose a repeatable sync method: partner integration, data feed, or API.
Keep product details and availability fresh and resolve diagnostics quickly.
Keep return policy, shipping eligibility, and storefront data consistent with the catalog.
Treat the Meta catalog as a downstream projection of one canonical product source, not a manually edited database.

items.title: Publish commerce content for agents, not just browsers
items.summary: A content architecture for publishing the same authoritative fact as HTML, Markdown, JSON, feeds, and protocol resources.
steps: Store content as structured records with provenance and verification dates.
Render human HTML from those records instead of duplicating facts in templates.
Offer JSON and Markdown alternates at predictable URLs.
Publish llms.txt as an index, not as a replacement for canonical source records.
Provide a searchable API and NDJSON bulk export.
Expose the same graph through MCP resources/tools.
Use source freshness rules so stale instructions can be flagged automatically.

items.title: Choose the right agentic-commerce protocol
items.summary: A practical map: use MCP for tools/resources, A2A for agent collaboration, UCP/ACP for commerce flows, and AP2/x402/MPP for payments depending on the use case.
steps: Need an agent to use your tools or read authoritative resources? Start with MCP.
Need independent agents to discover and collaborate with each other? Evaluate A2A.
Need merchant discovery/cart/checkout/order interoperability? Evaluate UCP and the commerce surfaces your target platforms actually support.
Need OpenAI-specific merchant/product discovery integration? Track ACP and OpenAI merchant feed requirements.
Need authorized agent payments? Evaluate AP2 in the relevant commerce flow.
Need machine-pay-per-request economics? Evaluate x402 or MPP.
Do not implement every protocol by default; implement the smallest set that maps to an active distribution channel.
